land.text: the imperial principality of the Swabian Hohenzollerns (partition of the County of Hohenzollern 1576; princes from 1623) (without the Hechingen cell)

predecessors.note: The state is older than 1806 (infobox: partition of the county 1576, raised to a principality 1629 or 1623); the dossier starts with Cliopatria's first shape and the sovereign Confederation membership.

land.text: the principality, annexed by Prussia and merged with Hohenzollern-Hechingen as the Province of Hohenzollern (without the Hechingen cell)

keyframe_review.note: 1,219 km2 (5 grid cells) in Cliopatria, but the shape is both Hohenzollern principalities, not Sigmaringen alone: the cell at 9.04E 48.34N lies inside the Hohenzollern-Hechingen keyframe (disc 8.97E 48.35N, 10 km; gazetteer: intersect of this shape with the disc = 1 cell), which the principality-of-hohenzollern-hechingen dossier already claims for 1576-1849. The Province of Hohenzollern page gives 1,142 km2 (1939) for the merged province of both principalities and no separate figures ('The article does not give the area of either principality'): the shape's 1,219 to 1,310 km2 matches that figure for both (ratio about 1.07 to 1.15), so the surplus is not a grid effect but the second principality. The correction removes the Hechingen cell (4 cells, about 1,012 km2 at the 253 km2 cell size). The Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen page gives no area and records no 1806 gain; the mediatisation page's undated table row 'Prince of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen | Prince of Fürstenberg: Jungnau & Trochtelfingen; Prince of Thurn and Taxis: Strasberg & Ostrach' names the lordships mediatised into it (not in the gazetteer, no year on the page), so no gain event is written. The shape stands for 1806-1810.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape without the Hechingen cell: Sigmaringen and its lands; the shape as drawn is both Hohenzollern principalities, and Hohenzollern-Hechingen has its own dossier (keyframe: a 10 km disc at 8.97E 48.35N)

keyframe_review.note: 1,310 km2 (the same 5 cells as 1806; the polygon area grows by about 90 km2 between 1806 and 1811 but the cells do not change, and no opened page dates a gain). Like 1806, the shape holds both principalities: it contains the Hechingen disc (8.97E 48.35N, 10 km) as 1 cell, and 1,310 km2 is 1.15 times the 1,142 km2 of both together (Province of Hohenzollern infobox, 1939). The correction removes that cell. The Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen page records no change of territory between 1806 and 1849; 'sovereign state again in 1815' as a member of the German Confederation (to 1849).

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape without the Hechingen cell: Sigmaringen and its lands in 1811-1848; Hohenzollern-Hechingen is its own dossier
the Cliopatria shape without the Hechingen cell, unchanged for 1849 to 5 April 1850; from 6 April 1850 the same land is Prussian (Hohenzollern Lands, seat Sigmaringen)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria runs the shape to 1852, but the principality ended in 1850: 'a treaty of annexation ... signed on 7 December 1849; the two princes abdicated the same day' and 'The Prussian state took possession of Sigmaringen on 6 April 1850' (the Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen page: 'annexed by Prussia, effective in March 1850'). The shape is right for 1849 to 5 April 1850 and wrong for 1851-1852, when the land is the Prussian Hohenzollern Lands (no Cliopatria Prussian shape for 1851-1852 contains it). The shape is also both principalities (see _1806): the Hechingen cell is removed here too; Hechingen was taken on 8 April 1850 (Province of Hohenzollern page).

region.text: the principality of the Swabian Hohenzollerns around Sigmaringen (Cliopatria shape without the Hechingen cell)

ledger.note: 1806: a sovereign member of the Confederation of the Rhine. The treaty of 12 July 1806 names Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen among the co-founders; the Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen page: 'a realm of the Confederation from 1806 to 1813', princes since 1623 (the infobox says 1629) and a seat at Sigmaringen Castle. The page names no boundary.

region.text: the principality, after the deposition of its ruler in 1848 (Cliopatria shape without the Hechingen cell)

ledger.note: 1849: Prussian troops arrive. 'Its ruler, Charles, was deposed in the revolutions of 1848'; 'Prussian troops arrived in August 1849'. The page does not call it an occupation; the hatching runs to the annexation.

region.text: the principality (Cliopatria shape without the Hechingen cell)

ledger.note: 1850: the occupation becomes annexation when Prussia 'took possession of Sigmaringen on 6 April 1850'.

region.text: the whole principality, annexed by Prussia (Cliopatria shape without the Hechingen cell)

ledger.note: 1850: Prussia takes Sigmaringen. 'In May 1849 he approved a treaty of annexation that was signed on 7 December 1849; the two princes abdicated the same day'; 'The Prussian state took possession of Sigmaringen on 6 April 1850 and of Hechingen on 8 April.' The Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen page: 'annexed by Prussia, effective in March 1850' (the 1850 date is the same; March against 6 April disagree).

region.text: the principality (Cliopatria shape without the Hechingen cell)

ledger.note: 1850: the principality ends. With Hohenzollern-Hechingen it became the Prussian Province of Hohenzollern ('Incorporation into Prussia: 1850', infobox), administered from Sigmaringen; the province was dissolved in 1946.

certainty.note: A small scattered Swabian principality; no page opened gives a boundary, and at the 253 km2 grid cell the corrected shape is four cells. The Prussian annexation of 1850 is a treaty date.

sources.title: German mediatisation
sources.note: Recess of 25 Feb 1803 (Bavaria: Augsburg, Bamberg, Freising, Passau, Wurzburg; Dalberg's Regensburg electorate with Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar); Confederation of the Rhine 1806. Undated table row: Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen with the mediatised Fürstenberg lands Jungnau and Trochtelfingen and the Thurn und Taxis lands Strasberg and Ostrach.

sources.title: Confederation of the Rhine
sources.note: 12 July 1806 founding and member joining dates (Wurzburg 23 Sept, Saxony 11 Dec 1806, Lippe 11 April 1807); dissolved 4 Nov 1813.

sources.title: Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
sources.note: Confederation of the Rhine 1806-1813; sovereign 1815; Prussian troops Aug 1849; annexation treaty Dec 1849 effective 1850.

sources.title: Province of Hohenzollern
sources.note: Annexation treaty 7 Dec 1849; Prussia took Sigmaringen 6 April 1850; 1,142 km2 (1939). The 1,142 km2 is the province of both principalities; Hechingen taken 8 April 1850.

notes:
END YEAR: identity.end is 1850/4 (Prussia took possession 6 April 1850), not the 1852 of Cliopatria's last row; the shape _1849 is adjusted to 1849-1850 and no state owns the land in Cliopatria's 1851-1852 (the Kingdom of Prussia row has no shape for 1851-1852 that contains it): the eu-09 Prussia writer should add the Hohenzollern Lands from April 1850.
START: the principality existed from the partition of 1576; 1806 is Cliopatria's first shape and the Confederation of the Rhine accession (12 July 1806, Confederation page).
UNVERIFIED: no page gives the principality's area or boundary. The 1806 mediatisation gains are not dated on any opened page: the German mediatisation page has an undated table row giving Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen the Fürstenberg lands Jungnau and Trochtelfingen and the Thurn und Taxis lands Strasberg and Ostrach (none is a gazetteer place), and its 1806 table does not list Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen; Achberg and Hohenfels are on no page opened. No gain event is written. Rulers omitted: the infobox gives only the first (Johann 1623-1638) and last (Karl Anton 1848-1849).
CONFLICTS: annexation 'effective in March 1850' (Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen page) against possession on 6 April 1850 (Province page); 1623 against 1629 for the elevation to principality.
Page budget 1-2: Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen and Province of Hohenzollern, plus the shared Confederation and mediatisation pages.
HECHINGEN: Cliopatria drew both principalities as one shape (1,142 km2 for both on the Province of Hohenzollern infobox against the shape's 1,219-1,310 km2); the shape contains the one cell of the principality-of-hohenzollern-hechingen keyframe (disc 8.97E 48.35N, 10 km), so every correction and ledger region here subtracts that disc. Hechingen keeps its own dossier (no Cliopatria row).
